Subject: Pilot SLA question — streaming TTFT vs sustained token guarantees

Hi Jordan / team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — BluePeak is excited to kick off the pilot. Before we spin up the dedicated pilot capacity we need one clarification from legal/ops: our product mixes interactive streaming prompts (customer chat) and longer-generation analytics jobs. The legal team flagged two competing expectations in the draft SOW: a strict time-to-first-token (TTFT) requirement for streaming endpoints and a separate sustained tokens-per-second expectation for analytical workloads.

Specifically: can Redwood provide an explicit carveout that differentiates the SLAs for the streaming endpoint vs the non-streaming endpoint? BluePeak's concerns:
- For interactive chat, TTFT matters (users abandon if first token > ~350ms).
- For long generations, throughput (tokens/sec) is the KPI (we can tolerate initial delay if sustained throughput is predictable).

Questions:
1) If we use the streaming endpoint for both types during the pilot, can you guarantee both a 95th-percentile TTFT and a sustained token/sec floor? If not, what fallback options do we have (route to sync endpoint, cost/billing changes, degraded ordering guarantees)?
2) How do you measure TTFT for streaming when requests are served across warm and cold caches? Do you provide a cold-start carveout?
3) What credit or rollback mechanics would apply if sustained throughput shortfalls persist for >1 hour?

I've attached a short diagram of our pilot traffic split (bluepeak-pilot-mapping.pdf) for context. Legal looped contracts@bluepeak.ai on this thread.

Thanks,

Samir — thanks for the clear note and the traffic split. Quick response and a proposed approach below.

Short answer: yes — we can support a tailored carveout, but it requires explicit measurement windows, agreed test prompts for TTFT, and a fallback routing policy that you sign off on.

Proposal (v0.1):
- Dual SLA model for the pilot:
  * Streaming interactive SLA: 95th-percentile TTFT <= 350ms for the "interactive" request class defined in the SOW (see example prompts).
  * Long-generation SLA: sustained throughput >= 1.5 kTokens/sec for the reserved worker pool over 5-minute sliding windows.
- Fallback policy: when a node's prefix cache is cold and can't meet both SLAs simultaneously, traffic designated as "analytics" will be routed to a sync (non-streaming) variant that satisfies the throughput SLA. Interactive traffic remains on streaming with lower burst capacity.
- Billing/credits: missed sustained-throughput (total pool average below floor for >1 hour) = prorated service credit for impacted hours. Missed TTFT (95p breach over a 24h window) = one-time credit plus investigation priority.
- Measurement: TTFT measured at token-emit event at the edge with request correlation id. We'll provide measurement scripts and test harness for your team.

I'll attach a short draft amendment with these bullets (proposed-sla-amendment-v0.1.pdf). Aditya: can you confirm whether the runtime can expose "warm/cold" labels per session and whether we can provide a CSV export of probe results for the pilot? Vivek / Kimberly: please flag any commercial/legal caveats.

Best,

Adding technical detail from runtime side — Samir, Jordan: good framing. A few practical notes we should agree on before we formalize measurements.

1) Warm vs cold: our serving runtime can emit a "warm" flag when a request hits a node that has a warmed KV cache for the model & prompt prefix. Typical TL;DR: first-ever requests after a scale-up or model load show higher TTFT. We can:
   - Provide a separate TTFT baseline for "cold" requests (e.g., 95p cold <= 800ms) and a tighter baseline for "warm" (95p <= 300ms).
2) Probe windows: recommend a 10-minute probe run on representative prompts to establish baseline for the pilot; we'll run probes from the same region as your users.
3) Graceful pacing: for very long generations we can stream an initial chunk (meeting TTFT) and then pace subsequent token emission to hit sustained throughput. That preserves perceived interactivity while keeping backend cost predictable.
4) Telemetry hooks: we can surface per-request telemetry (ttft_ms, warm_flag, tokens_emitted, tokens_per_sec) to your telemetry endpoint as part of the pilot.

If BluePeak wants to avoid dual endpoints during integration complexity, we can offer the above fallback logic inside the streaming endpoint with explicit labeling and billing rules.

- Aditya (Infrastructure, Redwood)

Thanks all — a few legal / procurement points to include in the amendment:

1) Measurement methodology must be explicit: TTFT computed at emitter edge with UTC timestamps; 95th percentile calculated over a rolling 24h window and over the sample of requests matching the "interactive" classification.
2) Test prompts: we need to agree on a 50-prompt canonical set (provided by BluePeak) used for acceptance testing and periodic SLA validation.
3) Credits & remedies: sustained-throughput shortfalls that last longer than 60 minutes trigger an auto-credit equal to (hours impacted * monthly committed rate * 0.05) — subject to a maximum per incident cap. Repeated incidents escalate to the enterprise reliability team and may trigger termination rights after three failed remediation periods.
4) Canary & acceptance: we should demand a one-week canary run for final acceptance metrics before the SOW signature.

I attached a short draft (sla-carveout-terms-draft.docx) with redline suggestions. Jordan / Aditya: please review the measurement hooks and confirm we can produce the required logs for a legal audit.
